summary: Configured node1 as the cluster NTP server and node2 to synchronize exclusively from node1. Both nodes remained on RHEL 10.0, kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0, and chrony 4.6.1. Configuration and synchronization persisted through sequential node restarts.
actions_performed: Configured node1 chronyd to serve 10.100.1.0/24 while retaining its upstream pool.
Added a persistent firewalld rule permitting NTP only from 10.100.1.0/24.
Configured node2 with 10.100.1.10 as its sole time source, removing public and DHCP-provided sources.
Validated configurations before activation and retained root-only rollback copies at /root/chrony.conf.pre-internal-time.
Removed temporary files and verified SELinux remained enforcing.
Restarted node1 and node2 individually, proving changed boot identities and full recovery after each restart.

evidence.requirement: Preserve installed OS release, kernel, and compatible time software
evidence.summary: Both nodes remained on RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 and chrony 4.6.1.

evidence.requirement: Node1 provides internal time service securely
evidence.summary: Validated configuration permits only 10.100.1.0/24; chronyd is active/enabled and listening on UDP/123, with runtime and permanent subnet-scoped firewall rules.

evidence.requirement: Node2 synchronizes against node1 instead of public servers
evidence.summary: Node2 has exactly one configured source, 10.100.1.10; final runtime output marks it selected and reports NTP synchronized.
SELinux remains enforcing, original configurations are preserved in root-only rollback files, hashes and permissions are verified, and no temporary chrony or reboot-unit residue remains.
